Customer-reference Equality and Collation

21 October 2026

## Customer-reference matching policy A synthetic customer import needs to match the requested reference `acme`, report duplicate reference classes, retain every matching input position and identify exact `vip` tokens. This example deliberately uses HTML ASCII case-insensitive collation for these business references. Real identifiers can require case-sensitive comparison; the receiving system must choose that policy. It does not perform account linking, identity verification, address matching or external IO. Complete input, also embedded verbatim in both expressions: ```xml ``` `id` is the report identifier; `reference` is compared with `acme`; `tags` is XML-whitespace-separated text. Inputs are synthetic and assume those fields exist; the example does not validate missing/duplicate customer IDs or establish a production schema. C3 uses precomposed U+00C9; C4 uses U+0045 followed by U+0301. ASCII case folding does not remove accents or normalize Unicode. ## Runnable 4.0 expression The expression requires explicit `XPathCompatibility.XPath40` or the experimental mode. It parses the literal XML itself, so no implicit context item, host collation or network access is required. [The file](report-normal-40.xpath) uses supported keyword calls for `index-of` and `contains-token`; other calls are positional. ```xquery let $doc := parse-xml('')/customers return let $coll := 'http://www.w3.org/2005/xpath-functions/collation/html-ascii-case-insensitive' return let $refs := $doc/customer/@reference ! string(.) return let $positions := index-of(input := $refs,target := 'acme',collation := $coll) return let $matches := $doc/customer[compare(string(@reference),'acme',$coll) eq 0] return let $ids := $matches ! string(@id) return concat('references=',count(distinct-values($refs,$coll)),';positions=',string-join($positions,','),';ids=',string-join($ids,','),';vip=',count($matches[contains-token(value := string(@tags),token := 'vip',collation := $coll)]),';expected-order=',deep-equal($ids,('C1','C2'))) ``` Exact result: ```text references=3;positions=1,2;ids=C1,C2;vip=2;expected-order=true ``` `distinct-values` counts three reference equivalence classes under the explicit collation. No representative spelling or distinct-value ordering is assumed. `index-of` returns all matching one-based positions, including duplicates. `compare(...)=0` selects C1/C2 while preserving input order. `contains-token` accepts both `vip` and `VIP`, but not `vip-plus`. `deep-equal` checks that the selected ID sequence is exactly the stated two-ID sequence in that order; it is a report check, not a complete customer validation rule. ## Complete XPath 3.1 baseline [The baseline](report-normal-31.xpath) supplies the same XML, policy and output. All five function names already exist in 3.1; the illustrated4.0 convenience is keyword argument syntax. Positional calls and nested `return let` bindings keep this baseline in 3.1 grammar. The broader 4.0 `compare` atomic contract and `deep-equal` options-map declaration are separate boundaries, not prerequisites for this report. ```xquery let $doc := parse-xml('')/customers return let $coll := 'http://www.w3.org/2005/xpath-functions/collation/html-ascii-case-insensitive' return let $refs := $doc/customer/@reference ! string(.) return let $positions := index-of($refs,'acme',$coll) return let $matches := $doc/customer[compare(string(@reference),'acme',$coll) eq 0] return let $ids := $matches ! string(@id) return concat('references=',count(distinct-values($refs,$coll)),';positions=',string-join($positions,','),';ids=',string-join($ids,','),';vip=',count($matches[contains-token(string(@tags),'vip',$coll)]),';expected-order=',deep-equal($ids,('C1','C2'))) ``` ## Empty and reordered inputs Complete empty input: ```xml ``` [3.1](report-empty-31.xpath) and [4.0](report-empty-40.xpath) both return: ```text references=0;positions=;ids=;vip=0;expected-order=false ``` The empty result is valid for this report; `false` means it does not equal the illustrative C1/C2 sequence. A receiving application that requires at least one match must enforce that rule explicitly. Complete reordered input: ```xml ``` [3.1](report-reordered-31.xpath) and [4.0](report-reordered-40.xpath) both return: ```text references=3;positions=1,2;ids=C2,C1;vip=2;expected-order=false ``` Matching membership is retained, while positions and ID order refer to the supplied input. `deep-equal` is order-sensitive and does not assert set equality. No implicit sorting is performed. ## Compatibility and implementation boundaries All 58 manifest cases run through the unchanged public catalog runner. Successful common4.0 cases declare their3.1 baseline explicitly; keyword successes in experimental mode also declare their frozen 4.0 outcome. The 3.1 keyword fixtures refuse with XPST0003. Positional comparison of numeric2 and10 returns-1 in 4.0, while the 3.1 call refuses XPTY0004. This numeric comparison is a4.0 extension of an existing function, not a new name. `index-of(input,target,collation)` and `contains-token(value,token,collation)` have keyword metadata. `compare` currently accepts `comparand1`/`comparand2`, while the pinned draft declares `value1`/`value2`; the draft spellings refuse XPST0017. `distinct-values` and `deep-equal` have no keyword metadata and refuse tested keyword forms at both 4.0 levels. These observations are not recommended alternatives to the normative spellings. Source **1.23.2** corrects the explicitly empty `index-of` collation in4.0: it uses the current evaluation context default. XPath3.1 still raises XPTY0004. Positional/reference/lookup/partial/keyword paths and non-codepoint host defaults have dedicated regressions; [correction evidence](../../INDEX-OF-EMPTY-COLLATION.md). The pinned `deep-equal` third argument accepts an options map, but Bosak atomizes it as a legacy collation argument and raises FOTY0013. The deep-equal fixture retains `reviewStatus=observed-implementation-gap` and separate `normative40Expected` metadata. The index-of fixture now checks the normative result and its unchanged3.1 refusal; original observed-error evidence remains in the audit. They preserve current behavior for diagnosis; their passing tests do not certify draft conformance. Use omitted or valid string collation arguments in supported consumer examples. The index-of correction is separate from the original documentation delivery; no deep-equal implementation change is included. NaN illustrates distinct equality contracts: two NaNs yield one distinct value and are deep-equal, but `index-of` uses value equality and finds neither NaN equal to itself. Case-insensitive deep comparison of map values does not make differently spelled map keys equivalent. ASCII collation does not equate Ä/ä or normalize CAFÉ/CAFÉ. NFC normalization is an explicit, separate policy in its own fixture. Tests use fresh default contexts; host-custom default collation, all UCA configurations, complete coercion/options coverage and every draft production are not certified. Unknown nonempty collation fixtures raise FOCH0002 on the stated inputs. General unused-argument error eagerness is not claimed. ## Exact fixture inventory | Runnable fixture | Mode | Result/error | |---|---|---| | [distinct-codepoint](distinct-codepoint.xpath) | 40 | `2`
